title: Campaign Management 101: A Step-by-Step Process
summary: More campaigns, weaker results? Learn how campaign management helps enterprise teams plan, execute, and optimize campaigns.
body_text: Key Takeaways Campaign success depends less on creativity and more on how well planning, execution, measurement, and optimization work together. Fragmented teams, channels, and data create execution gaps that weaken campaign performance long before results are measured. Real-time analytics turn campaign management from a fixed plan into an adaptive process that responds to performance signals as they emerge. Standardized workflows and shared performance metrics help enterprise teams scale campaigns without sacrificing consistency or control. The strongest campaigns connect activity to business outcomes, making it easier to optimize budget allocation, improve ROI, and prove impact. Marketers are running more campaigns than ever, but volume is not translating into results. Campaign output increased 31% year over year , yet 87% of senior marketers reported campaign performance issues in the past year and nearly half considered killing a campaign early because it was underdelivering. The problem is rarely in the idea. It is how teams manage the campaign from brief to outcome. Campaign management connects planning, execution, and measurement, so teams allocate budget deliberately, adapt while campaigns are live, and prove impact to the stakeholders who fund them. This blog covers what campaign management is, its core components, and a step-by-step process for planning, running, and optimizing campaigns that perform. Table of Contents What is campaign management? Why is campaign management important? Core components of campaign management How to manage a marketing campaign from start to finish: A step-by-step process Campaign management best practices Real-world examples of successful campaign management Conclusion What is campaign management? Campaign management encompasses all the planning, execution, and optimization activities of a marketing campaign. It involves coordinating multiple elements that ensure a cohesive and impactful message reaches the target audience. An effective marketing campaign consists of core components such as budget, timelines, channels, audience segmentation, content strategy, etc. These channels work together to deliver a unified message and ensure that every marketing campaign element aligns with business objectives. How is campaign management different from marketing automation? Campaign management coordinates time-bound initiatives end to end, from brief and approvals to execution and reporting, across teams and channels. Marketing automation runs always-on, trigger-based work like lead nurturing and behavioral workflows. Most enterprise teams use campaign management as the operating layer and automation as the execution engine inside it. Helpful Resource: Sprinklr Marketing Strategic Handbook Why is campaign management important? Today, businesses face increasing pressure to deliver measurable marketing results. However, poorly managed campaigns may lead to wasted budgets, missed opportunities, and inconsistent messaging. A strategic approach to campaign planning helps enterprises navigate challenges while unlocking new growth opportunities. Marketing campaign management is important for: Optimized budget allocation: A well-defined plan ensures resources are utilized efficiently, maximizing ROI and minimizing wasted spend. Increased campaign success rates: A structured approach reduces errors, improves execution, and increases the likelihood of achieving campaign goals. Improved team collaboration: Campaign management fosters collaboration among different teams (marketing, sales, creative, etc.), ensuring a unified and consistent message. Data-driven decision-making: Real-time data and analytics allow for informed adjustments, enabling agility and maximizing campaign impact. Enhanced brand consistency: Ensuring a unified message and experience across all channels strengthens brand perception and customer loyalty. Core components of campaign management Effective campaign management requires balancing multiple moving parts to ensure success. The following are the core components of the marketing campaign process: 1. Strategy and planning This phase sets the foundation by aligning campaign goals with business objectives. It involves defining clear, measurable KPIs, identifying the right audience segments and selecting the most effective channels. For instance, A global tech company launching a new smartphone first analyzes customer data to define its target personas (e.g., young professionals looking for productivity features). They set KPIs, such as website visits, pre-orders and social engagement. Based on their findings, they prioritize YouTube and Instagram ads for visual storytelling and LinkedIn for professional outreach. 2. Budgeting and resource allocation Budget constraints often force marketing teams to make tough decisions. The key is to invest strategically rather than spread resources too thin. This includes cost planning and assigning roles and responsibilities across departments. Consider an online retailer planning a Black Friday sale that assigns some of its ad budgets to retarget past website visitors using Facebook Ads. They use AI-powered bidding to adjust ad spending in real time dynamically. The marketing and sales teams align messaging to ensure promotional emails match the paid ads. Why is campaign ROI hard to measure even with more data? Measuring campaign ROI is hard because data is fragmented, not scarce. When teams define metrics differently and campaign data sits across separate publishing, analytics, and CRM tools, activity gets tracked, but campaign impact never connects to revenue. To measure campaign ROI accurately, enterprise teams need a focused set of outcome-aligned KPIs in a single reporting layer. 3. Execution and deployment Even the best strategies fail without proper execution. A lack of coordination across teams and channels can lead to missed opportunities and inconsistent branding. Therefore, creative development, campaign scheduling, and cross-channel coordination are essential. For example, A SaaS company launching a new software feature schedules a phased rollout as: Week 1: Teaser emails and LinkedIn posts Week 2: Paid social and influencer partnerships Week 3: Product webinars and live demos They use marketing automation to send personalized follow-up emails to users who engage with the campaign, increasing conversion rates. 4. Performance tracking and optimization Campaigns must be continuously refined based on real-time insights. Static strategies lead to wasted ad spend and missed engagement opportunities. This consists of data analytics ad reporting, A/B testing and experimentation followed by real-time adjustments. A fashion brand running a TikTok ad campaign notices that ads featuring user-generated content (UGC) outperform polished studio ads. They shifted some of their ad budgets to UGC-based creatives mid-campaign, leading to a boost in ROI. Campaign management is about execution, agility, data-driven decisions and cross-functional alignment. Marketing leaders who continuously test, optimize and integrate the latest tools stay ahead in an increasingly competitive landscape. How to manage a marketing campaign from start to finish: A step-by-step process A well-structured marketing campaign process follows a clear roadmap, from setting goals to optimizing performance. Below is a step-by-step marketing campaign management process to run a successful campaign: 1. Define campaign objectives and KPIs Campaign objectives must align with overarching business goals, such as increasing market share, accelerating demand generation or improving customer retention. KPIs should be measurable and tied to revenue impact, customer acquisition cost (CAC) or lead-to-conversion rates. Defining revenue-driven objectives helps brands measure marketing impact. For example, a company looking to expand its D2C presence might focus on conversion rates from paid ads, customer acquisition cost (CAC) and return on ad spend (ROAS) as key indicators of success. Source For example, Liquid Death, a canned water brand, aimed to disrupt the bottled water industry by targeting younger audiences with edgy branding. The goal was to increase brand awareness and sales through viral content. The KPIs in this case may include social media engagement , retail expansion and direct-to-consumer sales growth. More to read: How AI is Changing Marketing: Must Know for Leaders 2. Conduct thorough audience research Enterprises must move beyond basic demographics and invest in deep audience research. This means understanding not just who your buyers are, but what motivates them—through firmographic data, behavioral patterns, and real-time customer sentiment . By segmenting audiences based on roles, needs, and decision-making behaviors, brands can create messaging that resonates with the right people, in the right channels, at the right time. Audience insights also help uncover untapped opportunities. For instance, Tecovas—originally focused on cowboy boots—expanded into Western-inspired loafers and accessories after identifying evolving customer preferences. By listening closely and adapting their offerings, they grew their brand without losing their core identity. This shows how audience research can impact not only content strategy but product direction and long-term growth. Source Image address Social listening tools bring even more value by capturing live customer feedback and competitor trends. These insights let marketers adjust messaging in real-time, address emerging needs, and stay ahead of shifting expectations. Ultimately, understanding your audience isn’t a one-off task—it’s a continuous advantage that drives relevance, personalization, and engagement across every touchpoint. 3. Develop a compelling campaign narrative A cohesive campaign narrative reinforces brand positioning and ensures message consistency across global marketing efforts. Companies must craft storytelling that aligns with customer pain points and value propositions. A brand aiming to position itself as an eco-friendly leader must ensure its marketing emphasizes sustainability efforts, ethical sourcing and environmental impact. It is important to structure messaging to address different customer journey stages (awareness, consideration and decision). It should monitor brand mentions, sentiment analysis and PR reach to understand what its customers feel about them. Source Image address McDonald's Grimace birthday campaign merged nostalgia with modern marketing, offering a limited-edition purple shake and compelling content. The campaign went viral, trending on Twitter for eight days and ranking among TikTok’s top hashtags. It’s a prime example of how aligning brand storytelling with audience emotions can create viral moments for your brand. 4. Choose optimal marketing channels Your campaign planning must leverage a cross-channel strategy. Choosing the right marketing channels isn’t about being everywhere—it’s about being effective . Start with your campaign goals and map them to funnel stages: use TikTok or paid social for awareness, email and search for conversions, and programmatic for scale. Then, layer in AI to dynamically reallocate spend based on real-time results—like ROAS or engagement—maximizing impact without guesswork. Smart brands test early, optimize often, and treat channels like a performance ecosystem, not isolated silos. Metrics like multi-touch attribution or CPA only matter if you know what’s driving them. Source Vuori tested reallocating ad spend to Facebook and Instagram Reels, reducing its cost per purchase by 17% . The success proves the importance of continuously optimizing marketing strategies to create more cost-effective, high-impact campaigns. Pro Tip: Coordinating content, ads and analytics across multiple platforms can be overwhelming. Without a centralized system, teams struggle with fragmented data, inefficiencies and inconsistent messaging. An AI-powered marketing platform helps bring structure to omnichannel campaigns. By centralizing planning, automating workflows and providing real-time insights, teams can stay aligned, optimize performance and maintain brand consistency. And without the extra manual effort. Source Image address Want to see it in action? Book a demo today to explore Sprinklr Marketing! 5. Create high-impact content and ad creatives Ad content must be optimized for performance, ensuring high engagement and conversion rates. AI-driven personalization ensures each audience segment receives tailored messaging. Coca-Cola used generative AI to create personalized marketing campaigns that resonated with different consumer segments across global markets. The AI analyzed customer interactions, purchase history and regional preferences to generate custom video ads, dynamic social media content and tailored email campaigns. Source Image address AI-driven insights revealed that Latin American audiences engaged 30% more with ads featuring vibrant visuals and culturally relevant music. By applying these insights, Coca-Cola increased social media engagement by 20%, improved targeted email conversion rates by 15% and boosted online sales by 25% during a seasonal campaign. 6. Develop a detailed budget and timeline Companies need flexible budgets that adapt to campaign performance. AI-powered allocation ensures the highest-performing channels receive optimal investment. For example, Large-scale events require meticulous financial planning to avoid overspending and delays. A well-defined budget and timeline keep operations efficient. Brands can implement performance-based budget allocation for maximum ROI. Further using a marketing calendar can be used to align global campaign schedules and resources. Source Image address FIFA planned the 2022 World Cup with a $220 billion budget, covering infrastructure, marketing and event logistics. The key allocations included $6.5 billion in stadium construction, $1.7 billion in operational costs, $200 million in team preparations and $440 million in prize money. A strict timeline ensured stadiums and facilities were completed years in advance, preventing last-minute overruns. Careful budget tracking helped optimize expenses while delivering a world-class event. Pro Tip: Siloed campaign data leads to inefficiencies and missed opportunities. Unifying reporting enables teams to track performance holistically, spot trends early and adjust strategies proactively. Instead of manually stitching together data, use AI-driven analytics to unify cross-channel insights. With automated reporting and business-specific metrics, teams can identify trends faster, optimize spend and drive better performance. Source Image address Want to transform your marketing insights? Request a demo today. 7. Track, analyze and optimize campaign performance Continuous performance monitoring ensures enterprise campaigns remain agile. AI-driven insights allow for automated bid adjustments, content refinements and budget reallocation. Enterprises launching new products need to track performance across multiple channels. Data-driven decisions help maximize impact and ROI by identifying the best-performing platforms and content. The objective is to improve ad efficiency and maximize conversions through data-driven optimizations, with KPIs including engagement rate, conversion rate and cost per acquisition (CPA). For example, Similarly, a global entertainment company optimized its Snapchat advertising strategy using Sprinklr Marketing . By A/B testing different ad optimization windows, the company achieved a 29% reduction in cost per signup and a 19% decrease in cost per purchase in just four weeks. This underscores the importance of tracking, analyzing and optimizing campaign performance to maximize campaign efficiency. Source When should you pause or kill an underperforming campaign? Pause when the problem is fixable (creative, audience, or budget) and you still have a runway. Kill it when spend keeps rising without movement on the primary metric, or when the assumption behind the campaign is wrong. Watch the sustained gap between spend and outcome, not a single bad day, and set that threshold before the launch. Campaign management best practices Successful campaign management integrates automation, personalization and cross-channel consistency. Here are five key best practices to drive measurable outcomes while managing marketing campaigns: 1. Align campaigns with business goals: Ensure campaigns support brand growth, lead generation or revenue targets while integrating into CXM strategies. A well-aligned campaign enhances brand positioning and long-term customer engagement. With Sprinklr Marketing , brands centralize campaign execution and track performance across channels. Further, AI-driven insights can optimize messaging and budget allocation, ensuring that every campaign contributes to business outcomes. Source 2. Data-driven optimization: Track KPIs like ROAS, engagement, and conversions to measure success. Leverage AI-powered insights to identify trends, optimize ad spend and refine messaging. 3. Advanced segmentation and personalization: Use AI to segment audiences based on behavior, demographics and preferences. Deliver hyper-personalized messaging to increase relevance and engagement. Automated personalization across multiple channels improves conversion rates and customer retention. For example, Sephora utilizes AI-driven quizzes like " Find Your Perfect Foundation " to gather customer preferences. The insights from these quizzes are then used to provide personalized product recommendations through social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook. Additionally, Sephora integrates this data into its Messenger bot to deliver tailored beauty tips and exclusive offers in real time. 4. Cross-channel consistency: Maintain seamless messaging across social, email, paid ads and offline channels. A unified brand voice builds trust and strengthens customer relationships. Sprinklr’s cross-channel capabilities help ensure consistency in content distribution and audience engagement. 5. AI and automation for scale: Automate workflows, budget allocation and content personalization to improve efficiency. AI-driven insights enable faster decision-making and better resource management. Smart automation allows enterprises to scale campaigns while maintaining agility. As marketing landscapes evolve, brands need scalable and agile campaign management strategies. AI-powered optimization, automation and cross-channel consistency enable teams to adapt quickly while maintaining efficiency. Real-world examples of successful campaign management Successful marketing campaigns blend creativity, data and strategic execution to gain audience engagement. Let’s explore a few campaigns from global brands and how they leveraged technology, cultural insights and consumer behavior to maximize engagement: 1. How McDonald’s leveraged influencer marketing & global fan culture for campaign success McDonald's sought to connect with younger audiences and reinvigorate its menu offerings. The fast-food giant collaborated with global K-pop sensation BTS to create a special "BTS Meal." This collaboration included exclusive packaging and was promoted heavily on social media, leveraging BTS's massive global fanbase. The campaign generated approximately 11.5 million social media mentions and achieved a potential reach of 74.6 billion, reflecting extensive global engagement. Also, following the BTS Meal launch, McDonald's Korea observed a 250% increase in Chicken McNuggets sales over four weeks. Source Image address The key takeaways: Strategic partnerships with popular cultural icons can drive significant buzz and attract new customer segments. Aligning with influential figures or groups allows brands to tap into established communities and enhance their relevance. 2. Allbirds: Sustainability-driven branding Allbirds built its brand around sustainability by using eco-friendly materials like merino wool and eucalyptus fiber while maintaining transparency about its carbon footprint. The company integrated these values into a performance-driven, multi-phased campaign executed in collaboration with Adidas, culminating in the launch of FutureCraft.Footprint —a low-carbon shoe with only 2.94 kg CO₂e per pair. The campaign was executed over a 12-month period and combined product innovation, digital storytelling, and staggered launches across key touchpoints. Teams worked cross-functionally across time zones, leveraging shared expertise: Adidas brought high-performance manufacturing and scalability, while Allbirds contributed carbon calculation methods and natural material design. The rollout began with a 100-pair limited raffle via Adidas’ Creators Club, building exclusivity and early buzz. This was followed by a targeted FW21 release of 10,000 pairs and a broader SS22 drop. Digital content focused on education and transparency—highlighting carbon metrics, material sourcing, and minimalist construction principles inspired by waste-reduction design frameworks. title: Gabelli Equity Trust 10% Distribution Policy Reaffirmed and Declared Second Quarter Distribution of $0.15 Per Share
summary: RYE, N.Y., May 14, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Board of Directors of The Gabelli Equity Trust Inc. (NYSE:GAB) (the “Fund”) reaffirmed and satisfied its...
body_text: RYE, N.Y., May 14, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Board of Directors of The Gabelli Equity Trust Inc. (NYSE:GAB) (the “Fund”) reaffirmed and satisfied its 10% distribution policy by declaring a $0.15 per share cash distribution payable on June 23, 2025 to common stock shareholders of record on June 13, 2025. The Fund intends to pay a minimum annual distribution of 10% of the average net asset value of the Fund within a calendar year or an amount sufficient to satisfy the minimum distribution requirements of the Internal Revenue Code for regulated investment companies. The average net asset value of the Fund is based on the average net asset values as of the last day of the four preceding calendar quarters during the year. The net asset value per share fluctuates daily. Each quarter, the Board of Directors reviews the amount of any potential distribution from the income, realized capital gain, or capital available. The Board of Directors will continue to monitor the Fund’s distribution level, taking into consideration the Fund’s net asset value and the current financial market environment. The Fund’s distribution policy is subject to modification by the Board of Directors at any time, and there can be no guarantee that the policy will continue. The distribution rate should not be considered the dividend yield or total return on an investment in the Fund. All or part of the distribution may be treated as long-term capital gain or qualified dividend income (or a combination of both) for individuals, each subject to the maximum federal income tax rate for long term capital gains, which is currently 20% in taxable accounts for individuals (or less depending on an individual’s tax bracket). In addition, certain U.S. shareholders who are individuals, estates or trusts and whose income exceeds certain thresholds will be required to pay a 3.8% Medicare surcharge on their "net investment income", which includes dividends received from the Fund and capital gains from the sale or other disposition of shares of the Fund. If the Fund does not generate sufficient earnings (dividends and interest income, less expenses, and realized net capital gain) equal to or in excess of the aggregate distributions paid by the Fund in a given year, then the amount distributed in excess of the Fund’s earnings would be deemed a return of capital. Since this would be considered a return of a portion of a shareholder’s original investment, it is generally not taxable and would be treated as a reduction in the shareholder’s cost basis. Long-term capital gains, qualified dividend income, investment company taxable income, and return of capital, if any, will be allocated on a pro-rata basis to all distributions to common shareholders for the year. Based on the accounting records of the Fund currently available, each of the distributions paid to common shareholders in 2025 would include approximately 2% from net investment income, 21% from net capital gains and 77% would be deemed a return of capital on a book basis. This does not represent information for tax reporting purposes. The estimated components of each distribution are updated and provided to shareholders of record in a notice accompanying the distribution and are available on our website (www.gabelli.com). The final determination of the sources of all distributions in 2025 will be made after year end and can vary from the quarterly estimates. Shareholders should not draw any conclusions about the Fund’s investment performance from the amount of the current distribution. All individual shareholders with taxable accounts will receive written notification regarding the components and tax treatment for all 2025 distributions in early 2026 via Form 1099-DIV. Investors should carefully consider the investment objectives, risks, charges, and expenses of the Fund before investing. For more information regarding the Fund’s distribution policy and other information about the Fund, call: Molly Marion (914) 921-5681 About The Gabelli Equity Trust The Gabelli Equity Trust Inc. is a diversified, closed-end management investment company with $2.0 billion in total net assets whose primary investment objective is long-term growth of capital. The Fund is managed by Gabelli Funds, LLC, a subsidiary of GAMCO Investors, Inc. (OTCQX: GAMI). title: The 5 Key Components of a Mental Health Check-In
summary: Regular mental health check-ins are as important as our physical health checks. There are five key areas of focus when conducting a mental health check-in that will help you assess and enhance your overall wellbeing.
body_text: Regular mental health check-ins are as important as our physical health checks. There are five key areas of focus when conducting a mental health check-in that will help you assess and enhance your overall wellbeing. Concentration Our ability to focus on and complete tasks or be present when engaging with others provides insights into how busy our minds are. When we are at our best, we are able to attend to others and to tasks without being pulled away by distractions. If you are struggling to tune in or are experiencing drifts in your attention, this could indicate that you are feeling stressed, are overburdened, or are experiencing burnout. Engagement When we are feeling good, we tend to seek out the company of others or join in activities, both socially and professionally. If you find that you are dreading or avoiding interacting with friends, family, and co-workers, this can indicate issues with overall wellbeing. Additionally, keeping yourself so busy that you do not have time to think can be a way of keeping intrusive thoughts at bay. Either type of avoidance is an indication that there is something you do not feel ready to cope with. Energy Changes in our energy provide an early warning system for threats to our mental health. When we are feeling overextended emotionally, it can take a toll on us physically. The more occupied our minds are with stress or other issues, the less energy we have. Feeling a sudden decrease in energy is often the first sign of being overwhelmed, stress, or unhappy. Sleep Changes in our sleep pattern, just like changes in our energy, can reflect distress. A racing, overburdened mind will have difficulty shutting down and allowing the body to rest, resulting in an increase in sleepless nights. Mood Regulation Our ability to display a consistent mood externally and maintain one internally are both facets of our ability to regulate our mood. In times of stress or sadness, it becomes more difficult to control both how we feel and how we express ourselves. This can manifest in us being curt or dismissive, as well as in us experiencing increased irritability. Struggling with mood regulation decreases our ability to experience positivity. Difficulties in mood regulation also impact our ability to think clearly and to avoid becoming hyper-focused on negativity. By taking the time to ask ourselves how we are doing in these five key areas of mental health, we can catch early warning signs that we need to seek some support. The earlier we catch signs that we are not okay, the easier it is to address whatever challenges we are facing. Conducting a mental health self-check can alert you that something is impacting your wellbeing. It is often the case that we don’t know what is at the root of our challenges. --------------------------- Therapy can help you discover, tackle, and overcome whatever issues are impacting your wellbeing. You don’t have to do this alone. We are here to help and support you. Book a session today and begin your healing journey. Written by Kisstopher Musick, Psychologist. body_text: The Mortgage Shopping Problem Buying a home should be exciting. Shopping for a mortgage? Not so much. title: What Is Gamified Commerce?
summary: Gamified commerce is the use of game mechanics—like quizzes, challenges, points, or swipe interactions—to make the online shopping experience more engaging, personalized, and memorable. It’s not about turning your store into a video game—it’s about tapping into the psychology of play to drive better results. Instead of
body_text: Gamified commerce is the use of game mechanics—like quizzes, challenges, points, or swipe interactions—to make the online shopping experience more engaging, personalized, and memorable. It’s not about turning your store into a video game—it’s about tapping into the psychology of play to drive better results. Instead of asking shoppers to scroll and click their way through a product grid, gamified commerce offers a dynamic, two-way interaction that feels more like a conversation and less like a sales pitch. Why Gamified Commerce Works At the heart of gamified commerce is a simple truth: humans love to play. Whether it’s curiosity, competition, or the satisfaction of “winning,” game-like experiences activate emotional drivers that boost engagement. When someone interacts with a brand through a game, they’re not just browsing—they’re participating. And that participation creates data. Every click, swipe, or answer reveals something about what the customer wants. That’s what makes gamified commerce so powerful—it doesn’t just entertain, it informs. Brands can use that behavioral insight to improve targeting, product recommendations, and even retention strategies. Real Impact, Not Just Novelty When done right, gamified commerce isn’t a gimmick. It’s a conversion engine. Brands using Playably’s game formats consistently see 30–50% higher performance compared to traditional pop-ups or static campaigns. Better yet, shoppers are more likely to redeem the offers they earn through games than ones that are simply handed to them. That emotional investment—earned through fun and choice—drives higher intent and greater brand affinity. It’s not about distraction. It’s about depth. Where to Start You don’t need to reinvent your entire store to embrace gamified commerce. A simple quiz on your homepage, a swipe-based product finder, or even an interactive ad unit can spark meaningful engagement. And with tools like Playably, brands can implement and test these experiences quickly, without needing to become game developers themselves. Gamified commerce is the next evolution of e-commerce—and it’s already changing how brands connect with customers at every stage of the funnel.

title: S’adapter au changement : garder une longueur d’avance dans un marché européen en mutation.
body_text: Home Resources Resources Download Center Guidewire Conversations Podcasts Blog Help and Support Insurance Technology FAQ Blog Blog All Blog Posts Best Practices Careers Customer Viewpoint Developers General Interest Partner Perspective Technology Trends Industry Trends General Interest S’adapter au changement : garder une longueur d’avance dans un marché européen en mutation En Europe, le secteur de l’assurance fait face à de multiples bouleversements, dont certains s’accompagnent de défis extrêmement complexes. Ces transformations vont des tensions géopolitiques de plus en plus imprévisibles à l’augmentation des coûts opérationnels, en passant par des événements climatiques de plus en plus graves et fréquents, ou encore par la manière dont l’adoption accélérée des nouvelles technologies – et de l’IA en particulier – contribue à refaçonner nos sociétés et nos économies. En outre, les assureurs doivent tenir compte de l’arrivée sur le marché de nouveaux concurrents et de nouveaux modèles d’assurance. Dans ce contexte perpétuellement changeant et jalonné de défis, comment évoluent l’opinion et la perception que les assurés ont de leurs assureurs, des technologies innovantes et des nouveaux produits et services que ceux-ci mettent en place pour gagner en efficacité et mieux répondre aux besoins de leurs clients ? Notre rapport intitulé « Baromètre Guidewire 2025 : Enquête auprès des assurés européens » apporte des réponses à ces questions, en mettant en évidence les derniers résultats d’une enquête qui étudie le comportement et les opinions des assurés depuis 2020. Cette année, l’étude a mis en lumière un revirement positif dans l’opinion que les assurés ont des assureurs. En effet, près d’un tiers d’entre eux considèrent que leur assureur les comprend, et disent apprécier les produits d’assurance qui leur sont proposés. De plus, tandis que les acteurs du secteur s’interrogent sur la manière dont l’intégration de l’IA générative et de l’automatisation pourrait transformer leur activité, près de quatre clients sur dix se disent à l’aise avec l’idée que leur assureur fasse appel à l’IA pour les aider à souscrire la police la plus adaptée à leurs besoins ou à déclarer plus efficacement un sinistre, sans intervention humaine – tout en émettant quelques réserves concernant la confidentialité et le contrôle des données. Les assurés européens expriment également leur inquiétude face à la multiplication des catastrophes naturelles, telles que les inondations ou les incendies. Cela les pousse à se demander si leur assureur pourrait les assister de manière plus proactive, en leur proposant notamment une protection contre les événements climatiques extrêmes lorsque celle-ci est nécessaire. Guidewire s’engage aux côtés des assureurs afin de les aider à s’adapter à ces profonds changements. Nos solutions technologiques – ainsi que celles proposées par notre riche écosystème partenaire – sont conçues spécifiquement pour permettre aux assureurs de suivre l’évolution rapide des attentes des assurés et du marché dans son ensemble. Notre plateforme puissante basée dans le cloud permet aux assureurs de gagner en agilité, en leur donnant les moyens de mieux comprendre et de mieux tarifer les risques, tout en les aidant à optimiser et à transformer leurs processus et à se montrer encore plus réactifs face aux attentes changeantes des consommateurs et aux nouvelles tendances du marché. Malgré tous les défis auxquels le secteur assurantiel est confronté, nous sommes persuadés que ces changements offrent aux assureurs des opportunités exceptionnelles de prospérer et de générer encore plus de valeur pour nos sociétés à l’avenir. Les tendances et les conclusions mises au jour dans le rapport 2025 nous donnent – ainsi qu’à nos partenaires et au secteur de l’assurance dans son ensemble – de nouvelles pistes de réflexion sur les voies à emprunter pour garantir la réussite et la croissance de nos entreprises. title: DouYu International Holdings Limited Reports First Quarter 2025 Unaudited Financial Results
summary: DouYu International Holdings Limited - Investor Relations
body_text: WUHAN, China , May 20, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- DouYu International Holdings Limited ("DouYu" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: DOYU ), a leading game-centric live streaming platform in China and a pioneer in the eSports value chain, today announced its unaudited financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2025 . First Quarter 2025 Financial Highlights Total net revenues in the first quarter of 2025 were RMB947.1 million ( US$130.5 million ), compared with RMB1,039.7 million in the same period of 2024. Gross profit in the first quarter of 2025 was RMB113.5 million ( US$15.6 million ), increased by 4.1% from RMB109.0 million in the same period of 2024. Loss from operations in the first quarter of 2025 was RMB26.1 million ( US$3.6 million ), reduced by 84.3% from RMB166.9 million in the same period of 2024. Net loss in the first quarter of 2025 was RMB79.6 million ( US$11.0 million ), reduced by 9.5% from RMB88.0 million in the same period of 2024. Adjusted net loss (non-GAAP)[1] in the first quarter of 2025 was RMB20.9 million ( US$2.9 million ), reduced by 75.6% from RMB85.7 million in the same period of 2024. Ms. Simin Ren , Co-Chief Executive Officer of DouYu, commented, "In the first quarter of 2025, we focused on advancing our strategic revenue diversification and cost-efficiency initiatives. The effective execution of these strategies improved our gross margin and significantly narrowed our loss from operations year-over year. We ramped up our commercialization collaborations with game developers and refined the operation and promotion of our voice-based business, driving continued growth momentum in our innovative business. We also initiated staged optimization of our traditional business's cost structure, dynamically adjusting our streamers' resources to better align content supply with the platform's evolving needs. While these adjustments may lead to fluctuations in our platform traffic and revenues period-to-period, we believe they are necessary steps to improving operational efficiency and supporting the Company's healthy, sustainable long-term development and growth." Mr. Hao Cao, Vice President of DouYu, commented, "In the first quarter, our game-specific membership service and voice-based social networking business delivered a strong performance, driving revenues from our innovative business, advertising and others up 60.2% year-over-year to RMB382.6 million . The momentum also boosted the contribution from these businesses to 40.4% of total revenues, up from 23.0% in the same period last year. Our cost structure and operational efficiency initiatives also began yielding measurable results, with gross margin reaching 12.0% in the first quarter, up 5.9 and 1.5 percentage points sequentially and year-over-year, respectively. Moreover, we reduced our net loss and adjusted net loss to RMB79.6 million and RMB20.9 million , respectively. Moving forward, by continuing to execute our strategy of "cost reduction, efficiency improvement and loss narrowing," we will enhance the Company's financial resilience, advance balanced business growth and create long-term value for our shareholders." First Quarter 2025 Operational Highlights In the first quarter, average mobile MAUs[2] were 41.4 million, down 8.7% year-over-year, which aligns with our content cost optimization strategy. This decline was largely due to fewer official tournament broadcasts and a reduction in related derivative content offerings on the platform. In the first quarter, the number of quarterly average paying users[3] for livestreaming-related business was 2.9 million, with a quarterly ARPPU of RMB216 . The decline in paying users mainly stemmed from adjustments in our operational strategies, the scaling back of our platform's low-ROI operational activities, and sustained weakness in consumer spending amid a soft macroeconomic landscape. In the first quarter, revenues from our voice-based social networking business reached RMB290.1 million . During the Chinese New Year holiday, we launched a series of targeted marketing campaigns, supported by highly efficient traffic distribution strategies that effectively boosted user engagement and payment conversion rates. Our average MAUs for voice-based social networking business for the first quarter were 498,400, with monthly average paying users[4] of 82,900. First Quarter 2025 Financial Results Total net revenues in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 8.9% to RMB947.1 million ( US$130.5 million ), compared with RMB1,039.7 million in the same period of 2024. Livestreaming revenues in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 29.5% to RMB564.5 million ( US$77.8 million ) from RMB800.9 million in the same period of 2024. The decrease was primarily due to decreases in both the number of total paying users and average revenue per paying user, as a result of fewer low-ROI operating activities held in the quarter and continued macroeconomic softness. Innovative business, advertising and other revenues (formerly known as advertising and other revenues) in the first quarter of 2025 increased by 60.2% to RMB382.6 million ( US$52.7 million ) from RMB238.8 million in the same period of 2024. The increase was primarily driven by higher revenues from our voice-based social networking service and game membership service. Cost of revenues in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 10.4% to RMB833.5 million ( US$114.9 million ) from RMB930.7 million in the same period of 2024. Revenue-sharing fees and content costs in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 11.1% to RMB705.6 million ( US$97.2 million ) from RMB793.9 million in the same period of 2024. For comparison purposes, we reclassified certain costs related to our innovative business from other costs to revenue-sharing fees for the first quarter of 2024. The decrease was primarily driven by a significant reduction in content costs as part of our cost structure optimization efforts, as well as a decrease in revenue-sharing fees due to lower livestreaming revenues. The decrease was partially offset by increased revenue-sharing fees related to revenue growth in our voice-based social networking service. Bandwidth costs in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 31.6% to RMB56 .4 million ( US$7.8 million ) from RMB82.5 million in the same period of 2024. The decline was primarily due to our bandwidth allocation advancement and a year-over-year decrease in peak bandwidth usage. Gross profit in the first quarter of 2025 increased by 4.1% to RMB113.5 million ( US$15.6 million ) from RMB109.0 million in the same period of 2024. The increase in gross profit was primarily driven by decreases in our content costs and bandwidth costs. Gross margin in the first quarter of 2025 was 12.0%, compared with 10.5% in the same period of 2024. Sales and marketing expenses in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 3.5% to RMB72.9 million ( US$10.1 million ) from RMB75 .6 million in the same period of 2024. The decrease was mainly attributable to a decrease in staff-related expenses. Research and development expenses in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 39.5% to RMB32.7 million ( US$4 .5 million) from RMB54.2 million in the same period of 2024. The decrease was mainly attributable to a decrease in staff-related expenses. General and administrative expenses in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 16.4% to RMB35.8 million ( US$4.9 million ) from RMB42.8 million in the same period of 2024. The decrease was mainly attributable to a decrease in professional fees. Loss from operations in the first quarter of 2025 reduced by 84.3% to RMB26.1 million ( US$3.6 million ) from RMB166.9 million in the same period of 2024. Net loss in the first quarter of 2025 decreased by 9.5% to RMB79.6 million ( US$11.0 million ) from RMB88.0 million in the same period of 2024. Adjusted net loss (non-GAAP), which excludes net loss excluding share of loss (income) in equity method investments and impairment losses and fair value adjustments on investments, decreased by 75.6% to RMB20.9 million ( US$2.9 million ) in the first quarter of 2025 from RMB85.7 million in the same period of 2024. Basic and diluted net loss per ADS 5 in the first quarter of 2025 were both RMB2 .64 (US$0.4). Adjusted basic and diluted net loss per ADS (non-GAAP) in the first quarter of 2025 were both RMB0 .7 (US$0.1). Cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and bank deposits As of March 31, 2025 , the Company had cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, restricted cash in other non-current assets, and short-term and long-term bank deposits of RMB2,308.8 million ( US$318.2 million ), compared with RMB4,467.8 million as of December 31, 2024 . The decrease was primarily due to a special cash dividend distribution of US$300 million in February 2025 . [1] "Adjusted net loss (non-GAAP)" is defined as net loss excluding share of loss (income) in equity method investments, impairment losses and fair value adjustments on investments, and impairment losses of goodwill and intangible assets. For more information, please refer to "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and "Reconciliations of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release. [2] "MAUs" refers to the number of active mobile users (exclusive of innovative business unless the context otherwise indicates) in a given period. Average mobile MAUs for a given period is calculated by dividing (i) the sum of active mobile users for each month of such period, by (ii) the number of months in such period. [3] "Quarterly average paying users" refers to the average paying users for each quarter during a given period of time calculated by dividing (i) the sum of paying users for each quarter of such period, by (ii) the number of quarters in such period. "Paying user" refers to a registered user that has purchased virtual gifts on our platform at least once during the relevant period. [4] "Monthly average paying users" refers to the monthly average number of paying users during a given period of time calculated by dividing (i) the sum of paying users in each month of such period, by (ii) the number of months in such period. "Paying user" refers to a registered user that has purchased virtual gifts on our platform at least once during the relevant period. [5] Every one ADS represents one ordinary share for the relevant period and calendar year. About DouYu International Holdings Limited Headquartered in Wuhan, China , DouYu International Holdings Limited (Nasdaq: DOYU ) is a leading game-centric live streaming platform in China and a pioneer in the eSports value chain. DouYu operates its platform on both PC and mobile apps to bring users access to immersive and interactive games and entertainment livestreaming, a wide array of video and graphic content, as well as opportunities to participate in community events and discussions. By nurturing a sustainable technology-based talent development system and relentlessly producing high-quality content, DouYu consistently delivers premium content through the integration of livestreaming, video, graphics, and virtual communities with a primary focus on games. This enables DouYu to continuously enhance its user experience and pursue long-term healthy development. For more information, please see http://ir.douyu.com . Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures Adjusted loss from operations is calculated as loss from operations adjusted for Impairment of goodwill and intangible assets. Adjusted net loss is calculated as net loss adjusted for share of loss (income) in equity method investments, impairment losses and fair value adjustments on investments and impairment losses of goodwill and intangible assets. Adjusted net loss attributable to DouYu is calculated as net loss attributable to DouYu adjusted for share of loss (income) in equity method investments, impairment losses and fair value adjustments on investments, and impairment loss of goodwill and intangible assets. Adjusted basic and diluted net loss per ordinary share is non-GAAP net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by the weighted average number of ordinary shares used in the calculation of non-GAAP basic and diluted net loss per ordinary share. The Company adjusted the impact of (i) share of loss (income) in equity method investments, (ii) impairment losses and fair value adjustments on investments, and (iii) impairment losses of goodwill and intangible assets to understand and evaluate the Company's core operating performance. title: SRM Entertainment Announces Closing of $5 Million Private Placement
summary: Dominari Securities is dedicated to helping clients preserve, grow and create new wealth by providing a full range investment advisory and wealth planning services.
body_text: SRM Entertainment, Inc. (Nasdaq: SRM) completed a private investment in public equity (PIPE) financing, raising $5 million in gross proceeds. Winter Park, Florida, May 27, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SRM Entertainment, Inc. (Nasdaq: SRM) (“SRM” or the “Company”), a leading provider of creative and high-quality licensed media-themed merchandise, announces today the closing of its previously announced private investment in public equity (“PIPE”) financing with an institutional investor for gross proceeds to the Company of $5,000,000, before deducting placement agent fees and offering expenses. Pursuant to the terms of the securities purchase agreement, the Company sold an aggregate of 5,000 shares of its Series A Convertible Preferred Stock, convertible into an aggregate of 8,928,571 shares of common stock at a conversion price of $0.56 per share (not at $0.50 per share as previously reported), and warrants, each having the right to purchase one share of common stock, to acquire up to an aggregate of 8,928,571 shares of common stock, subject to beneficial ownership limitations. The purchase price for one unit (consisting of one share of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock convertible into approximately 1,785 shares and the same number of warrants) was $1,000. The warrants issued at the closing of the offering are exercisable immediately at an exercise price of $0.65 per share and will expire two years from the date of issuance. The Company intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes, including working capital. Dominari Securities LLC acted as the sole placement agent for the PIPE financing. The securities being offered and sold by the Company in the private placement have not been registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"), or state securities laws and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") or an applicable exemption from such registration requirements. The securities were offered only to accredited investors. The Company has agreed to file one or more registration statements with the SEC covering the resale of the unregistered shares issuable upon the conversion of the Series A Preferred Stock and the shares issuable upon exercise of the unregistered warrants. This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction. About SRM Entertainment, Inc. SRM Entertainment designs, develops, and manufactures custom merchandise which includes toys and souvenirs for the world's largest theme parks and other entertainment venues. Many of SRM’s creative products are based on award winning multi-billion-dollar entertainment franchises that are featured in popular movies and books. SRM products are distributed worldwide at Walt Disney Parks and Resorts, Universal Parks and Destinations, United Parks and Resorts – SeaWorld, Six Flags and other attractions. SRM’s products are offered alongside popular rides and attractions in theme parks, zoos, aquariums, and other entertainment venues. SRM’s design team developed specialty dolls, plush and toys for one of New York City’s landmarks that features a popular holiday show. SRM’s design team is credited with creating popular products which have been successfully sold at specialty theme park events. SRM’s exclusive-patented Sip With Me cups feature fun, kid friendly Zoo, Sea and animal themed characters as well as licensed characters from Smurfs, ICEE and Zoonicorn. title: Intelligent Protection Management Corp. Attains Accredited Partner Status with HPE Private Cloud AI
summary: Jericho, NY – April 1, 2025 – ACCESS Newswire - Intelligent Protection Management Corp. (“IPM,” the “Company,” “we,” “our” or “us”) (Nasdaq: IPM), a managed technology solutions provider focused on cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure, is pleased to announce that it has been selected by Hewlett Packard Enterprise to be an accredited partner for its HPE Private Cloud AI solution.
body_text: Jericho, NY – April 1, 2025 – ACCESS Newswire - Intelligent Protection Management Corp. (“IPM,” the “Company,” “we,” “our” or “us”) (Nasdaq: IPM) , a managed technology solutions provider focused on cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure, is pleased to announce that it has been selected by Hewlett Packard Enterprise to be an accredited partner for its HPE Private Cloud AI solution. Jason Katz, Chairman and CEO of IPM, commented, “We are delighted to provide our clients with this exceptional AI capability, designed to rapidly enhance their business outcomes. We will continue to evaluate ways to help our clients implement AI solutions.” HPE Private Cloud AI is co-developed by Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Nvidia, providing access to a broad ecosystem of AI leaders, including leading global systems integrators (SIs) and professional services organizations. It is a purpose-built solution designed to provide fast and easy deployment of private AI applications with a focus on inferencing, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and fine-tuning. HPE Private Cloud AI delivers a unique cloud experience designed to accelerate data science productivity and time-to-business value. It delivers instant AI productivity by being ready to deploy within the IPM Private cloud in three clicks. Once available, multiple users have self-service access to a diverse set of Nvidia technologies and open-source tools and models, which has the potential to increase productivity by 90% through an evergreen, cloud-managed experience. Jason Katz, Chairman and CEO of IPM, continued, “The solution’s efficiency is highlighted by its deployment – a swift eight hours in IPM’s secure private cloud, and full operational capability in just one day. This environment managed by IPM, as enhanced by HPE Private Cloud AI delivers up to a 5x model throughput improvement and a 2x increase in AI developer productivity. Responding directly to the needs of our clients, this private cloud AI solution, in partnership with HPE and Nvidia, is set to strengthen our existing offerings and open new avenues for growth.” Becoming an HPE AI Private Cloud Certified Partner unlocks significant benefits, including access to specialized expertise, a deeper understanding of HPE’s AI solutions, and the ability to leverage these solutions to offer customers innovative AI-driven insights and accelerate their own AI journeys. ABOUT INTELLIGENT MANAGEMENT PROTECTION CORP. (Nasdaq: IPM) Intelligent Management Protection Corp. (“IPM”) is a managed technology solutions provider focused on cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure. IPM provides dedicated server hosting, cloud hosting, data storage, managed security, backup and disaster recovery, and other related services, including consulting and implementing technology solutions for enterprise and commercial clients across the United States. Our other products include ManyCam. The Company has an over 20-year history of technology innovation and holds 8 patents. For more information, please visit: www.ipm.com.
